dossier.title: Joseph's celestial dream and family response: Qur'an 12:4–5 and Genesis 37
dossier.chronological_background: Genesis 37 belongs to the Hebrew Bible's Joseph cycle; Qur'an 12 presents a sustained Joseph narrative in a different literary and theological arrangement. Composition/redaction of Genesis and dates of surviving manuscripts are separate questions; no precise dating adjudicated in this screening.

source_table.tradition: Hebrew Bible / Jewish and Christian reception
source_table.edition: Hebrew Masoretic text pending critical verification

dossier.similarities: Eleven stars and two greater celestial bodies bow in Joseph's dream; familial response and brotherly hostility frame subsequent events.
dossier.differences: Genesis has a preceding sheaf dream, a second celestial dream and Jacob's rebuke; Qur'an 12:4 begins with the celestial dream, and 12:5 depicts paternal caution against the brothers. The narratives differ in sequence and characterization.
dossier.variant_witnesses: Hebrew MT, Greek Septuagint, Syriac Peshitta and relevant Dead Sea Scroll fragments require passage-specific witness checks; do not assume a fragment contains Genesis 37.
dossier.dating: Ancient textual tradition predates Qur'an, but exact redactional strata and dates of surviving witnesses require scholarly verification; modern translation dates are not ancient composition dates.
dossier.interpretations: Shared Joseph narrative tradition is clear at the story level; precise literary transmission route, oral mediation and textual dependence remain unproven.
